33.title: Administration of the Local Universe
33.b0.ask: “If the Father does not rule a local universe directly, who leads it, and how?”
33.b2.p: In Paper 32 we watched a local universe grow, from scattered energy all the way to mortal man. Now Paper 33 shows how such a universe is actually governed once it has been built.
33.b3.p: The Universal Father most certainly rules over his vast creation, but in the administration of a local universe he functions only through the person of the Creator Son. Plans, policies, and administration are entrusted to the Creator Son, to the local universe Mother Spirit, and to their children. Together with his Spirit associate, the Son delegates executive power to Gabriel and jurisdictional authority to the Constellation Fathers, System Sovereigns, and Planetary Princes (33:0.1).
33.b4.p: Who, then, are the father and mother who lead this universe? And in what order are executive, judicial, and legislative work divided, so that justice reaches all the way down to mortals like us?
33.b8.p: Our Creator Son is the personification of the 611,121st original concept of infinite identity, born at once of the Universal Father and the Eternal Son. His headquarters is the threefold mansion of light on Salvington, arranged that way because he has lived all three phases of creature existence: spiritual, morontial, and material. Because of his final bestowal on Urantia, he is sometimes called Christ Michael (33:1.1).
33.b9.p: Michael is not the Eternal Son, nor is he a member of the Paradise Trinity. Yet in his realm he holds all the divine attributes and powers the Eternal Son would show if he were present on Salvington, and more: he also represents the personality presence of the Father to this universe (33:1.2–1.3). That is why, to our universe and its worlds, the Sovereign Son is, to all practical intents and purposes, God (33:1.4).
33.b10.t: The supreme personality, our creator parent
33.b12.p: Among the Creator Sons, some resemble the Father more, some the Son; our Michael more resembles the Eternal Son (33:2.1). His power is limited only by the gravity circuits centering at Paradise and by the Ancients of Days, who keep for themselves all final judgments regarding the extinction of personality. Personality is the gift of the Father alone, but a Creator Son may initiate new creature designs (33:2.2).
33.b13.p: When Michael returned from his final bestowal on Urantia, the Creative Mother Spirit subordinated herself to him, and so he acquired jurisdiction over “⟦Q 33:2.3|33:3.5|21:4.5⟧all power in heaven and on earth⟦/Q⟧” (33:2.3). Their creature-bestowal experiences qualify the Michaels to portray the experiential divinity of the Supreme Being, and no other beings possess such qualifications for solitary sovereignty (33:2.4). When Michael is away from Salvington, Gabriel acts as regent (33:2.5).
33.b15.p: The Universe Mother Spirit of Salvington belongs to the sixth group of Supreme Spirits, the 611,121st of that order, and she volunteered to accompany Michael (33:3.2). The Son is the sovereign, but in all the details of management the Spirit is codirector, and the Son always grants her a co-ordinate position and equal authority (33:3.3).
33.b16.t: Enacts the role of a mother
Never defends authority, but always sustains the Son
Initiates the creation of certain universe children
Solely responsible for the orders of spirit personalities
33.b17.p: At the jubilee of jubilees, when the Creator Son is enthroned as a Master Son, the Universe Spirit for the first time makes public acknowledgment of her subordination to the Son (33:3.5). Michael in turn made the Spirit coruler, required all creatures to pledge loyalty to her as to himself, and issued the “⟦Q 33:3.6⟧Proclamation of Equality,⟦/Q⟧” declaring her his equal in personality and divine character (33:3.6).
33.b19.p: Now the Son and the Spirit preside over the universe much as a father and mother watch over their family of sons and daughters, and in no creative act does the one do anything without the counsel and approval of the other (33:3.7–3.8).
33.b21.p: The Bright and Morning Star is the highest spirit personality, born of the first joint act of the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit, and there is only one in each local universe (33:4.1–4.2). He embraces the divine will of the Son together with the creative imagination of the Spirit, and he understands both the seraphic hosts and mortal will creatures (33:4.3). He is not a creator, but he is a marvelous administrator; apart from creation and the giving of life, the Son and the Spirit never confer on important matters without him (33:4.4).
33.b22.t: Arbiter of all executive appeals concerning its administration
Nonpersonal affairs; carrying out mass judgments and resurrections
Commander in chief of the armies of heaven
May employ every order of celestial being in Nebadon
Takes Michael’s place when he is absent
33.b23.p: Gabriel and his staff are not teachers; they are administrators. During Michael’s bestowals Gabriel was the actual director of universe affairs, and he has been closely tied to Urantia ever since Michael’s mortal bestowal (33:4.7). Whatever order we belong to, when we become administrators we will come under Gabriel’s direction (33:4.8).
33.b25.p: The administration of Trinity-origin personalities ends with the superuniverses; the local universe is marked by the dual supervision of father and mother. Still, personalities from Paradise are present here too, and at their head is a Union of Days, Immanuel of Salvington. Because he is also the Universal Father’s representative to the court of the Creator Son, he bears the name Immanuel (33:5.1).
33.b26.p: Immanuel is so humble that he refuses all worship, and he is the only personality in Nebadon who has never acknowledged subordination to Michael. He gives counsel only on request (33:5.2). The Faithfuls of Days are sent to the constellations, and they too help only when asked (33:5.4).
33.b27.t: Universe headquarters; advises Michael only on request
Constellation headquarters; advises the constellation rulers only on request
33.b29.p: Gabriel is the actual administrator of Nebadon, and when he serves as regent he seeks Immanuel’s counsel on all major problems. Gabriel’s first assistant is the Father Melchizedek (33:6.1–6.2). Each of the subadministrations has its own field of concern (33:6.3).
33.b30.t: The physical and biologic status of living beings
Social and governmental conditions; unification and stabilization
The spiritual status of the realms
33.b31.t: Appointed by judicial decree; represent universes to other universes
Appointed by legislative decree; represent constellations within the local universe
Commissioned by executive decree of a System Sovereign; represent the system within the local universe
33.b32.p: Broadcasts from Salvington reach all inhabited worlds regardless of their spiritual status, but planetary intercommunication is denied to worlds under spiritual quarantine (33:6.5). Time, too, is reckoned differently at each level (33:6.7–6.9).
33.b33.t: Eighteen days, six hours, and two and one-half minutes
The Nebadon year (one hundred days of universe time)
Three days less 1 hour, 4 minutes, 15 seconds
33.b35.p: Michael is supremely concerned with only three things: creation, sustenance, and ministry. He takes no part in judicial work, for creators never sit in judgment on their creatures (33:7.1). The whole judicial mechanism is under Gabriel’s supervision, and every case is heard by two together: a judge of perfection antecedents and a magistrate of ascendant experience (33:7.2).
33.b36.t: Limits of the local universe courts
1. Questions of eternal life and death
The tribunals of Orvonton; sentences of extinction are carried out by the supergovernment
2. Default of a Son of God that jeopardizes his status
Requires the concurrence of the high assembly of the superuniverse
33.b37.p: In all other matters the courts of Salvington are final and supreme; there is no appeal (33:7.7). Human contentions on Urantia may sometimes seem unfairly settled, but in the universe justice and divine equity do prevail (33:7.8).
33.b39.p: There are no true legislative bodies on Salvington. The universe headquarters is concerned with adjudication, the constellations with legislation, and the systems with executive and administrative work (33:8.1). Salvington does have advisory councils; the supreme council is made up of three members from each system and seven representatives from each constellation, while systems in isolation may send only observers (33:8.3).
33.b40.t: The legislative assemblies on the headquarters of the hundred constellations
The System Sovereigns and their associates
The high advisory councils on Salvington
33.b41.p: If a recommendation of the high councils rests on the fundamental laws of the universe, the Nebadon courts rule on it; if it concerns local or emergency conditions, it passes to the constellation legislative assemblies and then to the system authorities for execution (33:8.5). All these courts and assemblies are spiritual transactions, very different from the institutions on Urantia that bear similar names (33:8.6).
33.b43.p: Paper 33 shows that a local universe is never run as the dictatorship of a single person. The Father rules through the Creator Son, and the Son raises the Mother Spirit to be his equal partner, giving us the pattern of the family. Gabriel handles execution, the courts handle judgment, the constellations handle legislation, and the systems handle administration, while the ambassador of the Trinity stands close by, advising only when asked. The weightiest questions, such as eternal life, are passed up to the higher courts of the superuniverse. Because authority is divided in this way yet never works at cross-purposes, even we mortals on a small planet can trust that in the end we will be treated justly and mercifully.
33.b44.t: To us, the Creator Son is, for all practical purposes, God
After his final bestowal Michael acquired all power in heaven and on earth
The Son and the Spirit care for the universe family as equal parents
The Bright and Morning Star leads the universe’s executive work and the heavenly hosts
Immanuel represents Paradise and advises only when asked
Systems, constellations, and the universe divide the physical, social, and spiritual realms
Creators do not judge; questions of life and death go higher
The universe judges, the constellations legislate, the systems execute
33.b46.box: The Father rules through the Son, and the Son with the Spirit; so in a well-ordered universe we are dealt with justly and mercifully.
34.title: The Local Universe Mother Spirit
34.b0.ask: “How does the Mother Spirit of the universe reach all the way down into our minds and lead us toward God?”
34.b2.p: In Paper 33 we saw the Creator Son and the Universe Spirit governing the local universe together, like a father and a mother. Now Paper 34 turns to the mother’s side: the local universe Mother Spirit.
34.b3.p: When a Creator Son is personalized, the Infinite Spirit individualizes a new and unique representation of himself to go with him into space. She becomes the Son’s companion, first in physical organization and later in the creation and care of creatures (34:0.1). In physical creation the Son provides the pattern, and the Spirit materializes it into physical substance (34:0.3).
34.b4.p: How did this Spirit become a distinct person? And through what circuits and ministries does she reach into the minds and lives of mortals, leading us out of the bondage of the flesh into the freedom of the spirit?
34.b8.p: When physical organization is complete, the Michael Son proclaims that life is next to be projected in the new universe. When Paradise recognizes this, the Master Spirit of that superuniverse disappears into the spiritual shining of the Deities and then reappears, and a tremendous spiritual flash takes place — the “primary eruption.” At the same moment, in the very presence of the Creator Son, a new personal representation of the Infinite Spirit personalizes: the Divine Minister (34:1.1).
34.b9.p: The technique of this event is a secret held in the bosom of the Trinity. Of one thing, though, we are certain: during physical organization the Spirit presence was incompletely differentiated from the Infinite Spirit, but now she acquires a personal nature tinged by that of the Master Spirit of her superuniverse (34:1.3). Because she was localized and personalized in this way, the Spirit could later become fully subject to the Creator Son (34:1.4).
34.b10.t: A less personal creative helper of the Son
Personalized as the Divine Minister with the primary eruption
The Mother Spirit, personally recognized by all
34.b12.p: Once the Creator Son becomes a Master Son, the personal qualities of the Creative Mother Spirit are so greatly augmented that she is personally recognized by all who contact her (34:2.1). From the beginning she has all the physical-control attributes of the Infinite Spirit, including antigravity, and once she becomes a person she exercises full control of mind gravity in the local universe (34:2.2).
34.b13.p: All Universe Spirits are basically alike in character, but their techniques of function vary according to the Master Spirit through whom they originated (34:2.3). The Spirit never fails the Son in creating and conserving creatures. When the Life Carriers provide the physical body, the Universe Spirit contributes the “⟦Q 34:2.5|28:5.21|36:6.4⟧breath of life⟦/Q⟧” (34:2.4–2.5). The presiding Spirit of Orvonton embodies the balanced union of all three Deities, so although our development is slow, we may look forward to an extraordinarily well-balanced creation in the ages to come (34:2.6).
34.b14.t: The first joint work of the Son and the Spirit
34.b15.h: 3. The Son and Spirit in Time and Space
34.b16.p: Neither the Eternal Son nor the Infinite Spirit is limited by time or space, but most of their offspring are (34:3.1). The Creative Spirit is wholly independent of space, equally and personally present everywhere in her universe, yet in her ministry to mind she must reckon with time (34:3.3–3.4). The Creator Son is the reverse: he is not handicapped by time, but he is conditioned by space and cannot be in two places at once (34:3.5).
34.b17.t: Limited — one place at a time
Limited in her ministry to mind
34.b18.p: So when the two work in administrative union, they are practically free of both time and space within their local creation, since each always has available the liberation of the other (34:3.6). Only absolute beings are independent of time and space in the absolute sense (34:3.7).
34.b20.t: The bestowal spirit of the Creator Son, the Comforter
The spirit circuit of the Divine Minister
The activities of the seven adjutant mind-spirits
34.b21.p: The Spirit of Truth is the spirit a bestowal Son pours out upon a world, drawing all truth seekers toward him who is the personification of truth (34:4.5). Wherever the Son may be, the Spirit of Truth functions undisturbed, because it is functionally centered in the Mother Spirit — and for that very reason, the Mother Spirit never leaves Salvington (34:4.6–4.7).
34.b22.p: The seven adjutant mind-spirits are the creation of the Divine Minister, and they minister to the minds of the human and subhuman orders (34:4.9–4.10). They are the “⟦Q 34:4.11|16:4.1⟧seven spirits of God⟦/Q⟧” the prophet saw before the throne (34:4.11). The adjutant of intuition helps the four control creatures of Salvington maintain directional control, and in all living beings a sense of orientation pointing north and south is forever fixed (34:4.12–4.13).
34.b25.p: On the inhabited worlds the Spirit begins with lifeless material and endows in turn vegetable life, animal organisms, and the first orders of human existence, leading the races of men toward higher ideals chiefly through the seven adjutants (34:5.2). When an animal mind becomes able to receive the adjutants of worship and wisdom, mind evolution crosses the threshold of spiritual ministry, and that mind is included in the circuits of the Holy Spirit (34:5.3).
34.b26.p: A mind touched by the Holy Spirit can choose to receive the Thought Adjuster, and once a bestowal Son has poured out the Spirit of Truth, all normal minds are prepared for the Adjusters (34:5.4). The Spirit of Truth depends largely on man’s personal reception, while the Holy Spirit is partly independent of the human will and partly conditioned by its co-operation (34:5.5).
34.b27.t: The Universe Daughter of the Infinite Spirit, the Mother Spirit
The Universe Son of the Eternal Son, the Creator Son
The Paradise Father, indwelling the mind
34.b28.p: The presence of these three spirits together is a symmetry of spiritual endowment, and it qualifies a mortal to realize consciously the faith-fact of sonship with God (34:5.7).
34.b30.p: Divinity may appear in many forms, but in human experience Deity is always one, and spirit influences of many origins are one in function (34:6.2). The divine Spirit comes down by a long series of steps to meet us as we are and where we are, and it never stops until it has carried the soul back up to the heights from which it came (34:6.3).
34.b31.p: Spiritual life, like physical energy, is consumed, so we need the renewing of the Spirit (34:6.5). Even the highest doctrine, held as dead theory, cannot change character; it comes alive only when the divine Spirit breathes upon it (34:6.6). It is not enough that the Spirit be poured out upon us; it must guide every phase of human experience. Souls watered in this way are all but independent of material environment in the joys of living (34:6.7–6.8).
34.b33.p: When we freely accept the Spirit’s guidance, an assurance of divine contact grows within us, and the Spirit bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God (34:6.12). In such a life the fruits of the spirit appear: love, joy, peace, long-suffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, and temperance (34:6.13).
34.b35.p: The flesh, which comes from animal-origin races, does not naturally bear the fruits of the spirit (34:7.1). Mortals on normal worlds do not suffer an acute conflict between spirit and flesh; their ascent is more like an educational training (34:7.2–7.3). Urantia’s struggle is unusually severe for two reasons (34:7.4–7.5).
34.b36.t: The loss of the moral support of a well-ordered society
The loss of a physical nature more responsive to spirit
34.b37.p: Even so, the faith sons who enter the spirit kingdom and do the Father’s will experience far less of this warfare, because Jesus showed mankind a new way of living (34:7.6). The natural desires of the body are not in conflict with even the highest spiritual attainment (34:7.7). So we should not doubt or fear failure (34:7.8).
34.b40.p: Paper 34 traces the Mother Spirit from a helper in physical creation, to a person with the primary eruption, and at last to the equal partner of the Creator Son. Through the seven adjutant mind-spirits she cares for the animal mind; as the Holy Spirit she embraces the mind that has crossed the threshold of worship and wisdom; and with the Spirit of Truth and the Adjuster she works as one within us. Because of the failures of Caligastia and Adam, the struggle between spirit and flesh is unusually hard on Urantia, but the Spirit does not force — she leads, and when we willingly co-operate, she brings forth the fruits of the spirit. At every dark crossroad the Spirit of Truth shows the way, so we can go forward without fear.
34.b41.t: With the primary eruption the Creative Spirit is personalized as the Divine Minister
The Mother Spirit controls mind gravity and gives the breath of life
3. The Son and Spirit in Time and Space
Together, the Son and the Spirit are free of time and space
The Spirit of Truth, the Holy Spirit, and the seven adjutants encircle the universe
The presence of three spirits lets us realize our sonship with God
The Spirit never forces; it leads and brings forth fruit
Urantia’s struggle is great, but faith is the victory that overcomes the flesh
34.b43.box: The Mother Spirit comes down to where we are, leads without force, and at every dark crossroad tells us, “This is the way.”
35.title: The Local Universe Sons of God
35.b0.ask: “Why do the Sons born in the local universe work closer to us than the Paradise Sons?”
35.b2.p: In Paper 34 we saw the local universe Mother Spirit become the equal partner of the Creator Son. Now Paper 35 introduces the first children the two of them bring forth together: the Sons of God of local universe origin.
35.b3.p: The Sons we met earlier were of Paradise origin. Nebadon has one Creator Son, Michael; its full quota of 1,062 Avonals; and an estimated fifteen to twenty thousand Trinity Teacher Sons (35:0.1). Just as triune Paradise Deity creates three orders of sonship, the dual Deity of the local universe, the Son and the Spirit, creates three high orders of Sons: the Melchizedeks, the Vorondadeks, and the Lanonandeks. After them come the Life Carriers, who are the subject of the next paper (35:0.2–0.7).
35.b4.p: What work does each of these local universe Sons do? And why has one order never once betrayed its trust, while hundreds of another have fallen into rebellion?
35.b8.t: Dual Deity of the local universe (the Son and the Spirit)
Dual Deity with the next level of God the Sevenfold
35.b9.p: From a new form of creative union between the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit came the original Melchizedek, the Father Melchizedek, who then worked with them both to bring the whole group of that name into being (35:1.1). In Nebadon he is the first executive associate of the Bright and Morning Star (35:1.2).
35.b10.t: The two are never away from Salvington at the same time
35.b11.p: All the Melchizedeks of Nebadon were created within one millennium. Because one of their own served as co-ordinate creator, they are partly of self-origin and form a self-governing order; they elect their own administrative chief every seven years (35:1.3).
35.b13.p: The Melchizedeks are the first order of Sons to come near enough to lower creatures to serve the evolutionary races directly, without incarnation. They stand about midway between the highest Divinity and the lowest creature life, so they are the natural go-betweens for the two. All forms of intelligent life find in them understanding friends, sympathetic teachers, and wise counselors (35:2.1).
35.b14.p: They show the highest type of true self-government, and not once throughout all Orvonton have they betrayed their trust (35:2.2). As the eldest sons of the family, they patrol the universe on their own initiative, make independent reports to the Creator Son, and go out as mobile advisory courts to settle the difficulties of the worlds (35:2.3–2.4). Twelve Melchizedeks accompany an Avonal Son on his bestowal (35:2.6).
35.b15.p: The Melchizedeks are nearly perfect in wisdom, but not infallible in judgment. When one errs in a minor matter while working alone, he goes to Salvington for instruction from the Creator Son and returns to service on the third day (35:2.8). Their number does not increase; upward of ten million are on record in Nebadon (35:2.9).
35.b17.p: The Salvington circuit of seventy primary spheres and 420 tributaries — 490 worlds in all — is called the Melchizedek University, and ascending mortals train on all of them before gaining residential status on Salvington (35:3.1). The 490 spheres are divided into ten groups, and the first group is supervised by the Melchizedeks (35:3.2).
35.b18.t: The home world of the Melchizedek Sons
The physical-life schools and the laboratories of living energies
35.b19.p: Every mortal who graduates from constellation training lands on the Melchizedek world, and you will never forget your first day there, not even after reaching Paradise (35:3.11). On the six tributary satellites of the pilot world, ascenders review in turn the stages of the journey they have already made (35:3.13–3.19).
35.b20.t: The early life on the world of mortal origin, in classes of those from the same planet
The experiences on the mansion worlds
The sojourn on the local system capital
The seventy tributary worlds of the constellation
The sojourn on the constellation headquarters world
Correlating these five epochs into one co-ordinated experience
35.b21.p: The College of High Ethics on the Melchizedek home world is presided over by the Father Melchizedek. Nebadon stands low in spiritual achievement, but its administrative troubles have made it a vast clinic for neighboring universes, so upward of one hundred thousand foreign students are always studying there (35:3.22).
35.b23.p: Together with the Trinity Teacher Sons, the Melchizedeks supervise the whole morontia education of ascending mortals (35:4.1). On Edentia they are known as emergency Sons, the first to act in every crisis, whether physical, intellectual, or spiritual (35:4.2, 4.4). They sometimes serve as temporary custodians of wayward planets, and seven times in Nebadon a Melchizedek has served in the likeness of mortal flesh (35:4.4).
35.b25.p: The Melchizedek known as Prince of Salem, who lived on Urantia in the time of Abraham, was one such case. With the approval of the planet’s Melchizedek receivers, who feared the light of life would go out in that time of spiritual darkness, he volunteered to incarnate, fostered the truth of his day, and passed it safely on to Abraham (35:4.5).
35.b27.p: The second order, the Vorondadeks, are more generally known as Constellation Fathers, because a Son of this order heads every constellation government. Nebadon has one million of them, and there is no known way for their number to increase (35:5.1–5.2).
35.b28.t: Less brilliantly versatile, but even more reliable as rulers
Not quite their administrative peers, but unexcelled in stability of purpose
Sometimes cited for error in technique, but never once in rebellion
35.b29.p: They serve as ambassadors to other universes and as consuls for the constellations, and of all local universe Sons they are most often entrusted with the full delegation of sovereign powers (35:5.5). A Vorondadek observer is usually present on isolated worlds and in an emergency may exercise absolute authority (35:5.6). Through all this service they have become the historians of the local universes (35:5.7).
35.b31.p: At least three Vorondadeks are assigned to each constellation, serving for 10,000 standard years, about 50,000 years of Urantia time (35:6.1). The hundred Constellation Fathers form the supreme advisory cabinet of the Creator Son (35:6.2).
35.b32.t: The reigning Most High, head of the government
Oversees spiritual affairs; acts for the Father when he is away
The physical welfare of the constellation
35.b33.p: At each change of administration the senior associate becomes head and the junior becomes senior, so each Most High serves on one constellation about 150,000 Urantia years (35:6.1). No major policy is carried out unless all three Most Highs agree (35:6.3), and our constellation, Norlatiadek, is now administered by twelve Vorondadek Sons (35:6.5).
35.b35.p: On the second group of the Salvington circuit, the seven Vorondadek worlds with their satellites — forty-nine realms in all — ascending mortals reach the height of their education in universe legislation (35:7.1). In the constellations they only observed the legislative assemblies; here they take part in enacting the general legislation that co-ordinates the pronouncements of the hundred constellations. This instruction is unexcelled even on Uversa (35:7.2).
35.b36.p: New activities await on these worlds that cannot be described in mortal words. The author says such revelation is not forbidden, but there are no words to convey its meaning and no human pursuits to compare it with (35:7.3).
35.b38.p: The third order, the Lanonandeks, are best known as System Sovereigns and Planetary Princes (35:8.1). Being lower in divinity, they were the first students of the Melchizedek University. Nebadon began with exactly twelve million Lanonandeks, who were divided into three classes in the final tests (35:8.2–8.3). Once classified, they cannot move to another class, and their number is fixed (35:8.7).
35.b39.t: System Sovereigns, assistants to the supreme councils, counselors
35.b41.p: Because the Lanonandeks draw nearer to the lower creatures, they give even greater service, but they also stand in greater danger of going astray. Still, especially the primary order, they are the most able administrators of the local universe, excelled only by Gabriel and his associates (35:8.15).
35.b43.p: System Sovereigns rule in commissions of two or three, and the Constellation Father names one as chief every dekamillennium (35:9.2). They are well-nigh sovereign in local affairs and are not supervised by Trinity observers, so theirs is the one place where disloyalty to Michael’s will could most easily take root (35:9.5).
35.b44.p: In Nebadon over seven hundred Lanonandeks have rebelled; only three were System Sovereigns, and nearly all the rest were Planetary Princes and tertiary Lanonandeks (35:9.6). This is no fault in creatorship. They were given great personal liberty so that they might better understand evolutionary creatures. Our high rulers hold that, though such Sons make trouble in the early ages, the higher loyalty of thoroughly tested Sons will far more than compensate for it (35:9.7–9.8).
35.b45.t: A new sovereign is installed within a comparatively short time
Instant isolation; the local spiritual circuits are severed
Only a bestowal Son can re-establish the lines of communication
May be rehabilitated, but never again in the position where he failed
35.b47.p: On the third group of the Salvington circuit, the seven Lanonandek worlds and their forty-two satellites, former System Sovereigns serve as administrative teachers. Here ascenders take part in actually co-ordinating the administrative pronouncements of the ten thousand local systems, and these colleges are excelled only by the schools of Ensa (35:10.1–10.2). The education sponsored by the Melchizedeks is practical and experiential — training in really doing the things being taught (35:10.3).
35.b48.p: Fallen Planetary Princes who accept rehabilitation serve here in custodial work, at least until Nebadon is settled in light and life (35:10.4). Yet many Lanonandeks have set wonderful records of service, and despite their tendency to err through the fallacies of personal liberty, they are a noble and loyal group (35:10.5).
35.b50.p: Paper 35 presents in turn the three orders of Sons born of the Son and the Spirit. The Melchizedeks are the most versatile teachers and emergency ministers, the pattern of self-government who have never betrayed their trust. The Vorondadeks rule the constellations with steady judgment and co-ordinate legislation. The Lanonandeks govern the systems and planets most closely and so give the greatest service, but having received great freedom, they also faced the greatest risk of falling. All these Sons are teachers of us ascending mortals as well; on the worlds of the Salvington circuit we learn ethics, legislation, and administration from them and practice them for ourselves. The Creator chose freely tested Sons rather than ready-made perfect ones, and that choice will in the end bear fruit in a deeper loyalty.
35.b51.t: A new union of the Son and the Spirit opened the Melchizedek order
The pattern and teachers of self-government, who have never betrayed their trust
In a university of 490 worlds, ascenders review the road behind them
Wherever help is needed, a Melchizedek is there
Rulers of steady judgment who have never rebelled
No constellation policy stands unless all three Most Highs agree
Here ascenders take part in real universe legislation
Those who come nearest also run the greatest risk of straying
The trials of free-choosing Sons are repaid by higher loyalty
Ascenders learn administration by actually doing it
35.b53.box: The local universe Sons teach and govern close beside us, and their loyalty, tested in freedom, makes the universe firm.
36.title: The Life Carriers
36.b0.ask: “Where does life come from, and how does it take root on a barren planet?”
36.b2.p: In Paper 35 we met the Melchizedeks, Vorondadeks, and Lanonandeks, the Sons born of the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit. Paper 36 takes up the fourth order announced at the end of that paper: the Life Carriers.
36.b3.p: Life does not arise on its own. It is constructed according to plans made by the Architects of Being, and it appears on inhabited planets either by direct importation or through the work of the Life Carriers. The Life Carriers design creature life and carry it to the planets, and after planting it they remain for long ages to foster its growth (36:0.1).
36.b4.p: What kind of beings are the Life Carriers? Who gives the spark of life to the matter they organize? And how does that life grow into beings with mind and will?
36.b7.h: 1. Origin and Nature of Life Carriers
36.b8.p: The Life Carriers are the only group of intelligent life in a local universe in whose creation the rulers of a superuniverse take part. They are the offspring of three: the Creator Son, the Universe Mother Spirit, and one of the Ancients of Days. The only beings who can decree the extinction of intelligent life also share in creating those who establish it (36:1.1).
36.b9.p: One hundred million Life Carriers were created in Nebadon. They are directed by the life-determining trio of Gabriel, the Father Melchizedek, and Nambia, the first-born Life Carrier (36:1.2). The Melchizedeks tested them and divided them into three divisions, and they always accompany the Life Carriers when they go out to plant life on a new planet (36:1.3).
36.b10.t: Subdivided into twelve groups of specialists in the forms of life
Study and assist in the protection and preservation of life
Specialists in handling and guarding the life patterns
36.b12.p: The fourth group of seven primary worlds in the Salvington circuit belongs to the Life Carriers, and each world has six satellites (36:2.1–2.9). The headquarters world holds the college of life planning, where teachers come even from Paradise, and the seven central emplacements of the adjutant mind-spirits are there as well (36:2.10).
36.b13.t: The study of universal life in all its known phases
Working out new modes of life organization
Developing ways to protect and preserve life
The evolution of creature life and its antecedents
5. The sphere of life associated with mind
The phases of mind correlated with life
6. The sphere of mind and spirit in living beings
The correlation of mind and spirit in organisms
Unrevealed domains related to the Supreme Being
36.b14.p: The domain of life is marked not by the decimal system but by three, seven, and twelve, and their combinations. Orvonton life patterns are configured as twelve inheritance carriers, and the human sex cells on Urantia contain forty-eight trait determiners (36:2.11).
36.b15.p: The original life designs come from the Creator Son, and the Life Carriers carry them out; any plan that departs from accepted formulas must be approved by the Creator Son (36:2.12). Urantia is a decimal planet, a life-experiment world — one in every ten — so a greater variation from the standard designs was allowed here (36:2.15). Even forms of life that seem useless are all needed for the full function of the higher intelligent life (36:2.17).
36.b17.p: Life does not appear spontaneously; the Life Carriers must initiate it on a barren planet (36:3.1). A corps usually consists of one hundred senior carriers, one hundred assistants, and one thousand custodians, and Urantia’s life was organized on the spot, after their arrival, according to approved formulas (36:3.2).
36.b19.p: The Life Carriers formulate the life plasm and stir matter as living catalysts, but the spark that enlivens the body and presages the mind comes from the Universe Mother Spirit. They pass on nothing of their own personal natures (36:3.4–3.5).
36.b20.t: What the Life Carriers may do
The implantation period (about half a million years)
Plant life and add new forms
Manipulate the environment and favorably direct evolution
Once a being with will appears
Their work ends; they may not interfere with will
They leave, though some may volunteer to stay as advisers
36.b21.p: On Urantia too, two senior carriers and twelve custodians took temporary renunciation vows and remained as advisers, and they are serving here still (36:3.9).
36.b23.p: In every local system of Nebadon there is one midsonite world where a Melchizedek has served as life carrier. There a materially modified Melchizedek Son mated with a Daughter of the material order, and their offspring are called midsoniters (36:4.1–4.2).
36.b24.t: Until one thousand standard years of age
Live as reproducing beings on their native world
Translated by seraphic transport; they lose reproductive prerogatives
None has experienced death; all are alive
The seventh world of the finaliters on Salvington
36.b25.p: Since they are not Adjuster indwelt, they are hardly immortal, yet they do not seem to be mortal either (36:4.4). The fifth group of the Salvington circuit is the worlds of the finaliters, and many zones there are closed even to ascenders (36:4.6–4.7). The finaliters decline to discuss the destiny of the midsoniters, but the Melchizedek life carriers believe their children will one day receive a transcendental spirit from God the Ultimate (36:4.8).
36.b27.p: Evolution on primitive worlds is purposeful, not accidental, because of the presence of the seven adjutant mind-spirits. They are the children of the Universe Mother Spirit and carry out her personal ministry to material minds (36:5.1). They are not separate personalities but more like circuits; they are in fact a level of consciousness of the Divine Minister (36:5.4).
36.b28.t: Quick perception, reflex instincts, sense of direction, self-preservation
Association of ideas; quick reasoning and judgment
Fidelity; the root of character and moral stamina
The curiosity of adventure and discovery; the scientific spirit
The social urge, species co-operation, the gregarious instinct
The religious impulse, the first mark that sets apart creatures with souls
The tendency toward progress, co-ordinating all the adjutants
36.b30.p: The adjutants grow experientially but never become personal. Because the first five function in animals, animals are to a certain extent indispensable even to man’s intellectual evolution (36:5.13). Mind is cared for by different ministers at different stages (36:5.15).
36.b31.t: Before it can learn from experience
The exclusive domain of the adjutant spirits
Supermind, encircuited in the Mother Spirit’s spirit cycles
36.b32.p: Even personal mind has no survival qualities apart from identification with spirit. Mind that works without spirit insight, without the ability to worship and crave survival, is not immortal (36:5.17).
36.b34.p: Life is both mechanistic and vitalistic, and it is not inherent in matter. The scientists of Urantia will understand protoplasm ever better, but they will never be able to produce living organisms (36:6.1). Life springs only from life, mind only from pre-existent mind, and spirit only from spirit ancestors (36:6.2).
36.b35.t: The initial spark, the breath of life
The Spirit of God (the Universe Mother Spirit)
The Mother Spirit, through the adjutant spirits
The personal impartation of the Mother Spirit
36.b36.p: When a plant or animal dies, its life survives only as part of the cosmic forces, without identity or personality; it does not survive as an individual. The survival of mortal creatures depends wholly on the evolving of an immortal soul within the mortal mind (36:6.5). Even the authors do not fully understand the source of the life-activation spark; they know only that life flows from the Father through the Son and by the Spirit (36:6.7).
36.b38.p: Paper 36 shows that life is not a product of chance but a gift that is designed, carried, and guarded. The Life Carriers organize the patterns and tend the environment, but the spark of life, the mind, and the power to reproduce come from the Mother Spirit. The seven adjutant mind-spirits lead evolution with purpose, from intuition to wisdom, and when the spirit of worship awakens, a creature becomes a candidate for spiritual ascension. The moment a being with will appears, the Life Carriers step back. From then on, our future rests on our own choices and on the immortal soul growing within our minds.
36.b39.t: 1. Origin and Nature of Life Carriers
Disseminators of life, in whose creation even the superuniverse rulers take part
On seven worlds life is designed, conserved, and studied
Life is given through them, and their work ends when will appears
The midsoniters do not die and are gathering for the future
From intuition to wisdom; worship is the badge of ascension
Life comes only from life, and the spark comes from the Spirit
36.b41.box: Life is conceived in the Father, expressed in the Son, and realized in the Spirit; our survival rests on the soul growing within the mind.
37.title: Personalities of the Local Universe
37.b0.ask: “What personalities stand beside us as we ascend, shaping this universe into one great school?”
37.b2.p: In Papers 35 and 36 we met the created orders of sonship in the local universe. Paper 37 continues from there. It deals chiefly with the Universe Aids, an intervening group between the ministering spirits and the ascending sons, and it also takes a brief look at the higher spirits stationed in Nebadon and at the permanent citizens of the local universe (37:0.2).
37.b3.p: At the head of all these personalities stands Michael, the Creator Son, and beside him the Divine Minister of Salvington, co-ordinate with him in divinity and complemental in creative attributes. In a very literal sense these two creators are the Father-Son and the Spirit-Mother of all the native creatures of Nebadon (37:0.1).
37.b4.p: Who, then, are the many personalities working under them? How do they help and teach us, the pilgrims of time? And who are the ones who stay beside us forever?
37.b8.t: The seven orders of Universe Aids
One in each universe; the first-born and chief executive
Superangels serving as Gabriel’s liaison officers
High spirits who foster creature survival and ascension
Volunteers from outside the local universe
37.b9.p: The Bright and Morning Star is the first-born of all creatures native to a local universe; in Nebadon he is Gabriel of Salvington. He is the personal representative of the Sovereign Son and the spokesman for his creative consort (37:1.9). In early times he worked almost alone, but as the universe grew he was given a staff of unrevealed assistants and, later, the corps of Evening Stars (37:1.10).
37.b11.p: The Evening Stars are superangels, planned by the Melchizedeks and brought into being by the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit; they serve chiefly as Gabriel’s liaison officers (37:2.1). Since Gabriel cannot be in two places at once, the Evening Stars represent him at the Salvington conclaves, as many as a thousand of which are often in session at the same time (37:2.2). On special missions to the planets they have sometimes been known as “⟦Q 37:2.3|93:9.7|96:1.9⟧the angel of the Lord⟦/Q⟧” (37:2.3).
37.b13.p: This corps is never closed to ascension candidates so long as the universe is not settled in light and life (37:2.4). On ascendant missions they always work in pairs, one created and one ascendant (37:2.7). They are the ranking personalities on the missions of Avonal bestowal Sons, and they administer the sixth group of the Salvington worlds (37:2.8, 2.10).
37.b15.p: The archangels are the offspring of the Creator Son and the Universe Mother Spirit, the highest type of spirit being produced in large numbers in a local universe; there are almost eight hundred thousand in Nebadon (37:3.1). They are one of the few groups not normally under Gabriel’s jurisdiction, for they are devoted not to routine administration but to the survival and ascension of mortals (37:3.2).
37.b16.p: Remarkably, a divisional headquarters of the archangels has been set up on Urantia in recent times. Visitors from outside soon learn that this small planet is Michael’s bestowal world, and their interest in it is immediately quickened (37:3.3). This points to a future gathering of other ascendant activities here and adds a solemn weight to the Master’s promise (37:3.4).
37.b18.p: A corps of one hundred archangels accompanies every Paradise bestowal Son, and two senior archangels serve as the Avonal’s personal aids. The one who announces the roll call at the end of a dispensation is the archangel of the resurrection, the “⟦Q 37:3.6|53:1.2⟧archangel of Michael⟦/Q⟧” (37:3.5–3.6). On the archangels’ worlds, the seventh group of the Salvington circuit, the personality record keepers preserve the records of personality between death and resurrection (37:3.7–3.8).
37.b20.p: The Most High Assistants are volunteers from outside the local universe, temporarily assigned as representatives or observers of the central and superuniverses; their number is always far up in the millions (37:4.1). Perfectors of Wisdom, Divine Counselors, Solitary Messengers, supernaphim, and others help bring Nebadon into fuller harmony with the ideals of Paradise (37:4.2).
37.b21.p: They work under the oversight of the Trinity ambassador, and when serving on request they often place themselves voluntarily under the jurisdiction of the directors of that realm (37:4.3). They serve in local universe and constellation capacities and are especially useful in grasping plans that call for more mature foresight (37:4.4–4.5).
37.b23.p: The High Commissioners are ascendant mortals who attained immortality by fusing not with an Adjuster but with a fragment of the Mother Spirit’s spirit. On certain worlds the Adjusters indwell mortals only temporarily and take eternal leave of them when life ends (37:5.1–5.2). These Spirit-fused mortals usually stop at Salvington and serve the local universe forever; they do not become finaliters, but they are enrolled in the local universe Corps of Perfection (37:5.2–5.3).
37.b24.t: A fragment of the Mother Spirit’s spirit
Paradise and the Corps of the Finality
Usually Salvington and the local Corps of Perfection
Deep experiential wisdom in Nebadon’s problems
37.b25.p: They begin as race commissioners on the planets, speaking for the viewpoints of the races and seeking mercy and justice for them; there are slightly over one and one-half billion in Nebadon (37:5.5–5.6). They sit as advisers in every tribunal and speak for those who cannot speak for themselves (37:5.7, 5.9). The eighth group of the Salvington circuit is their permanent home (37:5.10–5.11).
37.b27.p: Education in Nebadon is jointly administered by the Trinity Teacher Sons and the Melchizedeks, but much of the work of keeping it up and building it is done by more than three million Celestial Overseers. They are volunteers qualified by experience who range the universe as inspectors of school technique (37:6.1). From the worlds of human origin to the mansion worlds, the seventy realms of Edentia, and the 490 spheres of Salvington, the entire universe is one vast school (37:6.2).
37.b29.p: The method is to assign a task first and then teach the divine way to do it best; work and instruction go closely together (37:6.4). Mind and spirit grow together, and at last we no longer have to referee the conflict of spirit and flesh but enjoy a unified mind (37:6.6). Most Urantia mortals will have the chance to serve for a time in this corps before leaving Nebadon (37:6.7).
37.b31.p: The Mansion World Teachers are recruited and glorified cherubim, commissioned, like other teachers, by the Melchizedeks. They carry out most of the education of the morontia life, and their number is beyond the grasp of mortal mind (37:7.1). They are described more fully in later papers (37:7.2).
37.b33.p: Besides the power centers and physical controllers, high spirit beings of the family of the Infinite Spirit are permanently assigned to the local universe (37:8.1). One of them, Andovontia, the tertiary Universe Circuit Supervisor, isolated Urantia at the time of the Caligastia betrayal, and he sends greetings, expressing pleasure in the prospect of our restoration to the universe circuits (37:8.3).
37.b34.t: Help us overcome the handicaps of time and space
Supervises spirit and morontia circuits; isolated Urantia
Census Director; aware of the birth and death of will
Representative of the Supreme Executive of Orvonton
Traveling courts; about one hundred million commissions
About half a billion; living law libraries
Seventy-five seniors; almost four billion students
Seventy billion, ministering on the transition planets
37.b35.p: Each universe has its own native angelic corps, but it also receives help from higher spirits from outside. The present chief of Urantia seraphim is a primary supernaphim of Paradise (37:8.10).
37.b36.h: 9. Permanent Citizens of the Local Universe
37.b37.p: The local universe, too, has orders of permanent citizens who by and large neither ascend nor descend. Their growing experience continues to serve the universe at their level of origin (37:9.1–9.6).
37.b38.t: Offspring of the Son and the Spirit; close to the Spirit-fused mortals
A reproducing order; some become Planetary Adams
Custodians who keep planetary administration continuous
37.b39.p: The Material Sons are the Creator Son’s personalization of his last concept of being in dual form, male and female; this is the origin of the original Adam and Eve of each system (37:9.9). Mortals stay on their planet only briefly and celestial ministers come and go, but the midway creatures remain until the age of light and life, the actual custodians and citizens of the planet (37:9.11).
37.b41.p: Nebadon now has more than three million inhabited worlds, with ten million in prospect, and countless beings work on its 647,591 architectural spheres (37:10.1). The spironga, spirit offspring of the Morning Star and the Father Melchizedek, carry out routine spirit tasks, and the spornagia, an animal order of existence, care for the material side of the headquarters worlds (37:10.2–10.3).
37.b42.p: Ascending mortals who reach Salvington are assigned to nearly every celestial corps as helpers, students, observers, and teachers. From each level of achievement they reach back to give a helping hand to those who follow (37:10.5). This paper is only a brief outline of the personalities who make the universe a great training school, in which the pilgrims of time advance from world to world until they are lovingly sent on to Paradise and the destiny of the finaliters (37:10.6).
37.b44.p: Paper 37 unfolds a map of the many personalities who work under the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit. Gabriel and the Evening Stars carry on administration, the archangels foster survival and resurrection, the Most High Assistants come from outside to add their wisdom, and the High Commissioners speak for races who cannot speak for themselves. The Celestial Overseers and Mansion World Teachers make the universe one school, and the permanent citizens keep each level steady and continuous. And little Urantia, as Michael’s bestowal world, has become a headquarters for archangel activities. All these personalities work together for a single purpose: that the pilgrims of time may gain character through enlightened experience and go forward from world to world.

37.b47.box: The whole universe is one vast school, and countless personalities lead us to character through enlightened experience.
38.title: Ministering Spirits of the Local Universe
38.b0.ask: “Who are the angels who work beside us, and how is the gap between the material and spiritual worlds bridged?”
38.b2.p: In Paper 37 we surveyed the many personalities of the local universe. Now Paper 38 turns to the group that comes closest to mortals: the ministering spirits of the local universe. The personalities of the Infinite Spirit fall into three orders — angels, authorities, and powers — and the angels are the ministering spirits of time (38:0.1).
38.b3.p: As the supernaphim serve in the central universe and the seconaphim in a superuniverse, so the seraphim, together with the cherubim and sanobim, form the angelic corps of a local universe (38:0.2). The seraphim are very uniform in design; they are the most nearly standard of all spirit types of personal beings (38:0.3).
38.b4.p: How, then, are these angels born and trained, and what relationship do they have with us? And who bridges the great distance between humans bound to matter and pure spirit, and how?
38.b8.p: Seraphim are created by the Universe Mother Spirit. Ever since the “pattern angels” were made in the early times of Nebadon, they have been projected in unit formation, 41,472 at a time (38:1.1). While the Creator Son is engaged in creating the Material Sons, the Universe Mother Spirit undertakes her first solitary effort at spirit reproduction — and so begins the creation of the seraphic hosts (38:1.1).
38.b9.p: These angelic orders are projected at the time of planning for the evolution of mortal will creatures. Before that, the seraphim on duty in Nebadon were on loan from a neighboring universe (38:1.2). Because Nebadon is still in the making, seraphim are still being created periodically (38:1.3).
38.b12.p: Angels have no material bodies, yet they are definite, distinct beings. We cannot see them, but they perceive us as we are in the flesh. They share our nonsensuous emotions and sentiments, enjoy our music, art, and real humor, and know our moral struggles and spiritual difficulties well. They love human beings (38:2.1). They are not sex-emotion creatures, though they are deeply affectionate, and on the sex planets they are commonly called by feminine pronouns (38:2.2).
38.b13.p: In personal status angels are not far removed from humans, but in certain functions they far surpass us. They know things like the number of hairs on our heads without having to count them — true mathematical prodigies (38:2.3). Yet they are not our judges or accusers, and they are to be loved, not worshiped (38:2.4–2.5). When we are delivered from the flesh, we become very much like them (38:2.6).
38.b15.t: They share their places of rest and worship with us
The whole morontia and spirit ascent
An ideal fraternity and superb companionship
38.b17.p: Many orders of spirit beings work in the local universe that have nothing to do with the plan of Paradise ascension. In this paper the word “angel” is used only for the seraphic and associated offspring of the Universe Mother Spirit who are so largely concerned with the plans of mortal survival (38:3.1).
38.b18.p: Besides them there are six orders of unrevealed angels. They are never called seraphim or ministering spirits, and they are wholly occupied with the administrative and other affairs of Nebadon, which have no bearing on man’s spiritual ascent (38:3.1).
38.b20.p: The ninth group of the Salvington circuit — seven primary spheres, each with six tributary satellites, forty-nine worlds in all — are the worlds of the seraphim. The seraphim occupy only the first cluster exclusively; the other six are held by the six unrevealed orders of angelic associates (38:4.1). Here each seraphim has a real home, and a home means the dwelling of two seraphim, for they live in pairs (38:4.2).
38.b21.p: Seraphim are not male and female but negative and positive, and most assignments require two angels. Their pairing exists chiefly for function, not sex emotion (38:4.3). They gather for reunions every millennium; a seraphim who cannot leave her duty alternates attendance with her complement (38:4.4).
38.b23.p: Seraphic training is a long road that begins on Salvington and passes through the constellations and systems to commissioning. The first seraphim of Nebadon were trained by a corps of one thousand seraphim from Avalon; since then our angels have been taught by their own seniors. The Melchizedeks also play a large part in training all local universe angels (38:5.1).
38.b24.t: Noncommissioned observers on Salvington and its schools
Training on the seraphic worlds of the Salvington circuit
Mobilized in groups and units and assigned to a constellation
Serving as observers on the lowest evolutionary worlds
On the constellation’s associate worlds, preparing for system service
On the architectural worlds of a system capital, as ministering spirits of time
38.b25.p: Once commissioned, seraphim may range all Nebadon, even Orvonton, and their work is without bounds or limits. They are the point of contact between the beings of the spirit world and the mortals of the material realms (38:5.2–5.4).
38.b27.p: After their second millennium the seraphim are organized in units of twelve, and every level, from the smallest group to an angelic army, grows by multiples of twelve (38:6.1–6.2). These are the legions Jesus spoke of in Gethsemane when he said he could ask for “⟦Q 38:6.1|183:3.7⟧more than twelve legions of angels⟦/Q⟧” (38:6.1).
38.b28.t: An archangel or one of co-ordinate status
Brilliant Evening Stars or other lieutenants of Gabriel
38.b29.p: Gabriel is the “⟦Q 38:6.2⟧supreme commander of the armies of heaven,⟦/Q⟧” the chief executive of the Sovereign of Nebadon (38:6.2). Since Michael’s bestowal on Urantia, the seraphim and all local universe orders have been subject to the Master Son’s sovereignty, and when he was born in the flesh, a broadcast went out to all Nebadon: “⟦Q 38:6.3⟧And let all the angels worship him⟦/Q⟧” (38:6.3).
38.b31.p: Cherubim and sanobim are like the seraphim in all essential endowments and share their origin, though not always their destiny. They are the lowest order of angels and so all the nearer of kin to the human beings of the evolutionary worlds — affectionate and almost human (38:7.1). The two are inherently joined and serve in pairs (38:7.2).
38.b33.p: They are the routine spirit workers on the individual worlds of a system. In an emergency they may take the place of a seraphic pair, but they never act as attending angels to human beings; that is an exclusive seraphic privilege (38:7.3–7.4). Every fourth one is a quasi-material “fourth creature,” called a morontia cherubim, which does on the morontia worlds much what the midway creatures do on the evolutionary planets (38:7.6–7.7).
38.b35.p: Cherubim and sanobim too have paths of service that lead to higher status. By evolutionary potential they fall into three classes (38:8.1–8.4).
38.b36.t: By application and experience may attain full seraphic standing
Most remain as they are; the more gifted may achieve limited seraphic service
Keep their quasi-material nature and continue until the Supreme Being is factualized
38.b37.p: Many ascension candidates are attached to guardians of destiny; when their seraphic seniors leave them behind, they are embraced by the Universe Mother Spirit and become Mansion World Teachers (38:8.5). After long service they are re-embraced in groups of seven thousand and emerge as full-fledged seraphim. They may then become guardians of destiny, and the way lies open to Paradise and the Corps of the Finality (38:8.6).
38.b39.p: The midway creatures are classified with the ascending Sons of God, but in their work of serving mortal man they are reckoned with the ministering spirits of time (38:9.1). They are always found on life-experiment planets such as Urantia, and they are not an accident of evolution but part of the plans set in advance by the universe architects (38:9.2, 9.5).
38.b40.t: The modified staff of the Planetary Prince
The Adams and Eves or their immediate progeny
Varies by world, averaging about fifty thousand
Co-operation with the Adamic regime to advance civilization
38.b41.p: The gap between matter and spirit is bridged like a ladder of connected rungs. In the experience of an individual mortal, these many levels are unified by the mysterious work of the divine Thought Adjuster (38:9.9). Faithful midwayers will at last join the ranks of the ascending Sons and set out on the Paradise adventure together with the very earth brethren they have guarded (38:9.13).
38.b45.p: Paper 38 presents angels not as mysterious beings in a distant heaven but as companions beside us. The seraphim are born of the Universe Mother Spirit, commissioned after long training, and serve in a vast organization built in twelves, yet their hearts understand our struggles and love us. They do not judge us, and they do not accept worship. The cherubim and sanobim grow into seraphim through service, and the midway creatures, who work closest to us on earth, will in the end set out with us for Paradise. So the gap between matter and spirit is bridged without a break, and every link is gathered into one within the Adjuster who dwells in us.
38.b46.t: The Universe Mother Spirit projects them 41,472 at a time and creates them still
Angels love us but do not judge us, and they are not to be worshiped
Six orders unconnected with the ascent serve Nebadon’s administration
On forty-nine worlds the seraphim live in pairs

An organization growing by twelves, under Michael’s sovereignty

Through two embraces they may become full seraphim
The gap between matter and spirit is bridged by a series of links
38.b48.box: Angels do not judge us but love us, and every link from matter to spirit is joined for the sake of our ascent.
39.title: The Seraphic Hosts
39.b0.ask: “How do seraphim born of the same mother divide into seven kinds of service, and where do they finally arrive?”
39.b2.p: In Paper 38 we looked at the origin, nature, training, and organization of the seraphim. Now Paper 39 shows where those seraphim actually serve and what they do — the seraphic hosts at work. The Universe Mother Spirit intends to produce uniformly perfect seraphim, but for some unknown reason her offspring are very diverse, and after training they unfailingly fall into seven groups (39:0.1).
39.b3.p: That does not make any seraphim inferior to another. Every angel is at first limited to the service of her inherent group, but through experience and education she can gain skill in other services. Manotia, the supreme seraphim who helped prepare this paper, has achieved all seven services one by one (39:0.9–0.10). Strikingly, the higher an angel’s inherent level, the more persistently she seeks assignment to lower service, especially among the planetary helpers (39:0.11).
39.b4.p: Where, then, does each of these seven hosts serve, and what does it do? And how does all this service fit together with our own ascent?
39.b8.p: The supreme seraphim are the highest of the seven revealed orders of local universe angels, and they work in seven groups (39:1.1). Among them, the 144 bestowal attendants are completion seraphim who always accompany a Paradise Avonal on a bestowal mission; theirs is the highest local universe service open to seraphim who have attained Paradise (39:1.4–1.6).

39.b10.p: The court advisers are the defenders of mortals. Justice demands a ruling on every default, but mercy requires that each misstep be fairly judged in keeping with the creature’s nature and the divine purpose (39:1.8). The universe orientators help pilgrims leaving the local universe, who often feel something like homesickness, to realize that they stand not at the summit but at the very bottom of a long ladder (39:1.10–1.11). The Creator Son’s fourth bestowal was in the likeness of a teaching counselor (39:1.15).
39.b12.p: The superior seraphim are so named not because they are qualitatively superior, but because they are in charge of the higher activities of a local universe (39:2.1). They work in seven groups centered on Salvington (39:2.2).

39.b14.p: The transporters’ work touches us closely. Until we awaken on Paradise, ascenders depend on seraphic transport to go from world to world (39:2.10). Being enseraphimed is like sleep: you go to sleep for a set time and wake at the appointed moment, while the Thought Adjuster remains fully awake (39:2.11–2.12). Angels cannot carry bodies of flesh and blood, so we “⟦Q 39:2.13⟧sow a mortal body⟦/Q⟧” in the grave and “⟦Q 39:2.13⟧reap a morontia form⟦/Q⟧” on the mansion worlds (39:2.13).
39.b16.p: The supervisor seraphim are assigned to the service of the constellations and have their headquarters on the constellation capitals (39:3.1). The law forecasters show lawmakers how a proposed enactment would affect the lives of freewill creatures, speaking not for man’s passing desires but for the true longings of the evolving soul (39:3.3). In this way even mortal man may contribute to the evolution of universe law.

39.b18.p: The social architects become involved not when two beings work together, but when three or more do, for a group of three or more constitutes a social problem (39:3.6). Transport seraphim are not inanimate projectiles; they are fully aware of their speed and direction, and by using three lines of energy at once they reach average speeds of over 555,000 miles per second (39:3.8–3.9).
39.b20.p: The administrator seraphim handle the administration of the local systems (39:4.1). The justice guides prepare the defense in cases of mortal survival, making sure that unerring justice is dealt out with generous mercy (39:4.4–4.5). In the Lucifer rebellion very few justice guides were lost, but more than a quarter of the other administrator seraphim and lower seraphic ministers were misled (39:4.6).

39.b22.p: The quickeners of morality teach that loyalty is the fruit of an intelligent appreciation of universe brotherhood. As we ascend, first we learn to be loyal, then to love, then to be filial, and only then may we be free (39:4.11). They also show that this life is only the first link in a long chain, and that the way we do our work matters more than the work itself (39:4.13).
39.b25.p: The planetary helpers have their headquarters on the system capitals and serve chiefly the Planetary Adams (39:5.1). On Urantia most of them were withdrawn when the Adamic regime collapsed, but some still serve here in several groups (39:5.2). Vevona, chief of the souls of peace, is the angel who, when Michael was born, proclaimed “⟦Q 39:5.5⟧on earth peace and good will among men⟦/Q⟧” (39:5.5).

39.b27.p: The idea that angels have wings comes from traditions of people who saw seraphim being prepared for transport. What look like wings are in reality energy insulators — friction shields (39:5.12). The spirits of trust also help us see that uncertainty is the secret of contented continuity, the romance of an unknown future (39:5.9).
39.b29.p: The seraphim of transitional ministry serve wherever they can help creatures pass from the material to the spiritual estate. In Satania today they put their greatest effort into educating surviving mortals on the seven mansion worlds (39:6.1). More about them is told in the narratives of the mansion worlds (39:6.9).
39.b32.p: The seraphim of the future do not minister widely except on older and more advanced planets. Many are held in reserve near Salvington, preparing for the day when the age of light and life dawns in Nebadon. They minister chiefly to mortals who survive by modified orders of ascension (39:7.1). Since they are not now directly concerned with Urantia, their activities are not described (39:7.2).
39.b34.p: Some seraphim fulfill their destiny of service within the local universe, in high posts such as the Evening Stars, but Seraphington is always the eternal goal of all angels. It is the angelic threshold to Paradise, where the ministry of time passes into the service of eternity (39:8.1).
39.b35.t: Attain perfection as artisans, Technical Advisers, or recorders

39.b36.p: Angels are created “⟦Q 39:8.7⟧a little higher than you,⟦/Q⟧” so they cannot start from the very bottom of human existence; but they can go down to those who start there and guide them step by step to the portals of Havona (39:8.7). That is why the supreme choice of seraphim in the career of time is to become a guardian angel (39:8.5). Angels are not sure of their eternal future until they reach Seraphington, but no angel who has reached it has ever gone astray (39:8.9).
39.b38.p: For the angels who have reached the Father of spirits, the career of time is over. From then on they are the servants of God, the consorts of divine personalities, and the peers of the Paradise finaliters (39:9.1). Many completion seraphim return to their native universes to add the ministry of experiential perfection, and our own world enjoys the service of twelve specialized groups of them (39:9.2).
39.b39.p: Just as before Paradise they longed to be guardians of destiny, after Paradise they most desire to be bestowal attendants of the incarnated Sons. They remain devoted to the universal plan of starting mortal creatures on the journey to Paradise (39:9.3).
39.b42.p: Paper 39 divides the seraphic hosts into seven branches, but every branch points the same way. From the superior seraphim of Salvington to the helpers of systems and planets, they speak for mercy beside justice, help law reflect the true longings of the soul, and plant brotherhood, peace, and trust in primitive mankind. The more able an angel is, the more she wants to come down to a lower post, and the summit of her service is the path of the guardian angel who walks with a mortal. At the end of that path, the completed angels come back to us and remain our true friends forever. All this service teaches us one thing: wherever we are, to choose sincerely to do the will of God.

39.b45.box: Angels come down to lower places to walk with us, and they teach that the key to heaven is to choose sincerely, wherever we are, to do the will of God.
40.title: The Ascending Sons of God
40.b0.ask: “How does a lowly mortal of animal origin become a son of God — and do different destinies mean different measures of love?”
40.b2.p: In Papers 38 and 39 we met the angels and midway creatures who serve beside us. Now Paper 40 turns to those who receive that service: the ascending Sons of God on their way up to Paradise. These papers began with the Deities and have come down the scale of living beings until they reached the lowest order of life with the potential of immortality. The author himself is a Mighty Messenger who was once a mortal on an evolutionary world (40:0.10).
40.b3.p: Seven classes of ascending sons have been revealed (40:0.1–0.8). From the lowly animal-origin mortal to the Personalized Adjuster, their story is a glorious recital of divine love and gracious condescension throughout all the universes (40:0.9).
40.b4.p: On what grounds, then, are mortals like us called sons of God? How does the destiny of those who fuse with their Adjusters differ from that of those who do not? And does that difference mean there is a difference in the Father’s love?
40.b8.t: The seven classes of ascending sons

40.b9.p: The privilege of sonship is not reserved for mortals of animal origin. Guardian seraphim, through experience and service with ascending mortals, also achieve ascendant sonship; they attain Paradise through Seraphington, and many even join the Corps of Mortal Finality (40:1.1). For an angel to climb to the heights of finaliter sonship is a far greater achievement than our own survival with the help of the Adjuster (40:1.2).
40.b11.p: The Material Sons are by origin descending Sons — the Adams and Eves who come down from the system capitals to the inhabited worlds (40:2.1). When they fully succeed in their mission as biologic uplifters and their world is settled in light and life, they may resign their planetary duties and register as perfected Material Sons. They are then accredited as ascending Sons and begin the long journey to Havona and Paradise together with mortals (40:2.2).
40.b13.p: The midway creatures’ Paradise ascent is long deferred, but when a planet reaches the intermediate epochs of light and life, they are released from planetary duty. They are registered as ascending Sons and set out for Paradise by the very same routes as the mortal races (40:3.1).
40.b14.t: All enrolled in the Mortal Corps of Finality
40.b16.p: When a mortal fails to survive, it is never because the Adjuster neglected its duty. The deserted Adjuster returns to Divinington and may be sent again to the worlds of time. After repeated services of this kind, or after serving as the indwelling Adjuster of a bestowal Son, efficient Adjusters are personalized by the Universal Father (40:4.1).
40.b17.p: Originally prepersonal, they became experiential by taking part in the lives of lowly mortals. Because the personality they receive comes from the Father’s own bestowals of experiential personality, the Personalized Adjusters are the highest of all orders of ascending sons (40:4.2).
40.b19.p: Mortals are the last link in the chain of beings called sons of God. The touch of the Eternal Son comes down through personalizations ever less divine and more human until it reaches beings we can see and touch, while the Infinite Spirit reaches the limit of expression in the angels (40:5.1–5.2). The Father cannot step down in this way, but because he lives within us as the Adjuster, the one who is farthest from us in personality and spirit is the nearest of all (40:5.3).
40.b20.p: Spirit identification is the secret of personal survival, and mortals are classified into three series by their relation to the Adjuster (40:5.4). The differences among the three brain types are no factor at all in Adjuster bestowal or destiny; from the system headquarters on, all three progress alike (40:5.17).

40.b24.p: We are not yet by nature of the divine order; we are wholly mortal. Until fusion takes place, our status is that of faith sons of God (40:6.1). Yet it is a solemn and supernal fact that such lowly material creatures are the faith children of the Highest: “⟦Q 40:6.2|2:5.4⟧Behold, what manner of love the Father has bestowed upon us that we should be called the sons of God⟦/Q⟧” (40:6.2).

2. A Creator Son became our elder brother

40.b27.p: Adjusters are immortal spirits, and union with them confers eternal life on the soul (40:7.1). We are hardly yet ascending sons, but by faith and by freewill co-operation with the Adjuster we can attain that status. When we and our Adjusters are fused forever and the two become one, we are in fact ascending sons of God (40:7.2).
40.b28.p: Because the Father has given himself to us, he asks of us, “⟦Q 40:7.4|1:0.3|1:0.6⟧Be you perfect, even as I am perfect⟦/Q⟧” (40:7.4). Fusion with the Adjuster is a divine validation of eventual Paradise attainment, and Adjuster-fused mortals are the only class of human beings who all traverse Havona and find God on Paradise (40:7.5).
40.b30.p: Almost all survivors fuse with their Adjusters on the mansion worlds or the morontia spheres, but a few, even after “⟦Q 40:8.2⟧seventy times seven⟦/Q⟧” opportunities, never achieve oneness (40:8.1–8.2). If a court of inquiry finds the mortal not at fault, the Adjuster returns to Divinington and the mortal is fused with an individualized gift of the spirit of the Creator Son (40:8.3).
40.b31.p: Son-fused mortals are few — fewer than one million in all Orvonton. Apart from residential destiny on Paradise they are in every way equal to their Adjuster-fused associates, and on the training worlds of the superuniverse they are truly our brethren (40:8.4–8.5).
40.b33.p: Spirit fusion never occurs during life; it happens only at reawakening on the mansion worlds. There is no overlapping in fusion: a creature fuses with the Father, the Son, or the Spirit, never more than one (40:9.1). In these mortals, too, the Adjuster indwells during life and builds up the soul, but at death it departs, and its place is filled by the spirit of the Divine Minister (40:9.2–9.3).
40.b34.p: The difference lies in memory. Human memory survives because the Adjuster carries a transcript of it, but Spirit-fused mortals lack this mechanism and awaken as if newly created. Yet when angels retell their story and they consult the records, an experiential-recognition-response in the soul brings those events back to life (40:9.4–9.6). They are permanent citizens of the local universe, and their home is the eighth group of worlds around Salvington (40:9.9).
40.b36.p: The spirits of mortal fusion always ascend to their level of origin (40:10.1). These differences are no flaw in the ascension plan. If every mortal went on to Paradise, the local universes and superuniverses would depend entirely on those merely passing through, so it is fitting that each have a permanent ascendant citizenship (40:10.3–10.4).

40.b38.p: That destinies differ does not mean one is greater or lesser than another, only that they are different. The finaliters enjoy the widest service, but the intimate knowledge and authoritative wisdom of a single universe are gathered by the Spirit-fused veterans (40:10.5–10.6). God loves each of his sons individually and alike (40:10.13).
40.b41.p: Paper 40 shows the path by which angels, Adams, midwayers, Adjusters, and we mortals all rise as sons of God. In personality the Father is farthest from us, yet as the Adjuster he is nearest of all, and becoming one with that fragment is the guarantee of reaching Paradise. Even the faintest desire to co-operate with the Adjuster and to find God is enough for the soul to survive. The paths of fusion differ — some come to rest in the local universe, some in the superuniverse, some on Paradise — but this is not discrimination; it is a wise design for the whole universe. Every son receives the Father’s unlimited and unique love, and by faith we already enjoy that sonship now.
